author: WP12
summary: A short new chapter on cna-content builds: the single-file build, the dependency graph, SHA-256 fingerprints and --explain, atomic publication, worker determinism, XNB output and migration, and the scope of CNA's closeout evidence. Current at TARGET and already covered in depth by the Content Pipeline guide and pipeline internals; the hash and timestamp rule was added to the internals page as an expansion, and the XNB-to-CNB transcoding refusals and runtime comparisons now live on the XNB type-readers deep dive.

concepts.text: The cna-content CLI builds one source file or a directory tree, and a .contentproj drives the same coordinator through the build task, so command-line and project builds share one graph, fingerprint and publisher.
tokens: A .contentproj is not a second format with a second engine behind it

concepts.text: A single source file builds to one output whose extension must match --format (cna-content build ContentSource/Textures/wall.png -o Content/Textures/wall.cnb).
The output directory holds runtime artifacts, not the pipeline module; a game loads the logical name through ContentManager and never runs an importer at startup.
tokens: nothing in a shipped game needs the tool

concepts.text: Each graph node records its source, selected importer, processor and writer, normalised parameters, component identities, input dependencies, runtime references, primary artifact, bounded child outputs and deployment files.
Cycles, path escape, output collisions and duplicate ownership are errors; a cycle is reported once with its whole chain.
tokens: a cycle is found by an explicit-stack depth-first walk

concepts.text: The graph is deterministic: parallel scheduling may change completion order but not published names, bytes or manifests.
tokens: The output bytes are meant to be identical whatever the count

concepts.text: The manifest fingerprints file bytes, component identities and versions, normalised configuration, output format and codec settings with SHA-256.
A cache hit also validates the primary, child and support outputs; missing or tampered outputs force a rebuild.

File timestamps do not enter the fingerprint; the only timestamp comparison in cna-content is the PreserveNewest copy of .contentproj Content and None items, which sit outside the fingerprinted graph.
tokens: File modification times never enter it

concepts.text: --explain reports why a node was built or reused, separating source, dependency, parameter, component-version and output-integrity changes, and that reason state is a tested contract.
tokens: what lets --explain say why a node rebuilt

concepts.text: Writers finish artifact bytes before publication; each output is written to a temporary sibling and replaced atomically, so an interrupted build leaves the old or new file, never a prefix.
tokens: never a prefix of the new one

concepts.text: Directory builds publish and clean only graph-owned outputs: an unrelated .cnb in the destination is never discovered and deleted by extension, and cleanup refuses symlinks, escapes and changed digests.
tokens: a corrupt or old manifest is a reason to rebuild, not a license to delete files found in the output tree

concepts.text: A failed import, processor or writer leaves the previous valid artifact in place, and the manifest is written only when every item succeeded.
tokens: The manifest is written only when every item succeeded

concepts.text: Worker counts from 1 to 64 are supported; registries are frozen before execution and graph edges decide readiness in waves of at most --workers nodes.
tokens: Ready nodes run in waves of at most --workers

concepts.text: Repeated cold, no-op and dependency rebuilds are compared across worker counts, and performance measurements are kept apart from correctness gates as single-host developer evidence.
The pipeline emits XNB for supported types with selectable XNA platform, version, profile, compression and reader-name style; external references stay logical content references.
Migration can import a supported XNB and produce native CNB, with field-level runtime comparisons where both formats express the same object.
tokens: Those are the field-level comparisons behind the claim that migration preserves content

concepts.text: Not every XNB maps losslessly to frozen CNB schema 1: unsupported surface formats, reader graphs, shared resources outside Models, Xbox payloads and non-null Model tags are refused with a named boundary rather than silently normalised.
tokens: From XNB to CNB: what transcoding refuses
shared resources in any root except a Model

concepts.text: CNA's own closeout records component, differential, determinism, cache, custom-extension, sanitizer and fuzz, Windows and performance evidence; the site states these as CNA-reported and names what was not run.
concepts.note: Attributed to CNA rather than asserted; the Windows CI lane is described with its trigger limits.

concepts.text: The C++ custom-extension API remains experimental and third-party managed XNA processors are not loaded directly.
tokens: There is no assembly scanning in C++

concepts.text: Build success is not runtime proof: the produced asset must still be loaded and, for graphics and audio, engaged on an appropriate renderer or device route.
tokens: the proof is a round trip across the boundary
